title: Exact polynomial bulk resource ingress
objective: Make public dense ZZ[x] and QQ[x] construction use checked canonical host-list packing followed by one generated FlintByteRegion-to-owned-resource parse, preserving exact Sage semantics, portable fallback, lifecycle safety, and cross-host performance

oracles: SageMath ZZ[x] and QQ[x] construction and serialization

handoff.summary: Public dense ZZ[x] and QQ[x] list construction now performs checked whole-list canonical packing, one generated FlintByteRegion creation, and one transactional parse into an independent owned FLINT polynomial. The stream-sized BigInt transport and its obsolete C parser are removed. SagePack bytes and capability-disabled packed fallbacks remain compatible; sanitizer lifecycle tests, strict Python, architecture checks, portable tests, Linux x64 Sage differentials, 20001-coefficient scaling evidence, and macOS arm64 generated-resource evidence pass.
risks: The original <=2x same-host SageMath warm public-construction goal remains unmet: on the recorded AMD EPYC host ZZ[x] is 3.65x and QQ[x] is 20.69x SageMath at 5001 coefficients. Boundary copy plus parse is already small; QQ host coercion/object-model packing is the dominant measured follow-up.

The required Linux arm64 witness was not available during this lane. macOS arm64 on Apple M1 Max validates the arm64 generated-resource build and public path, but it is not a substitute for Linux arm64 CI evidence.

The M1 host had no usable SageMath command-line oracle, so its report intentionally contains Sage.js resource-path measurements only. Linux x64 reports contain the same-host Sage semantic and timing comparisons.

Windows x64 and Wasm continue through the tested capability fallback because these FLINT resource declarations still have wasm=False; native Windows generated-resource execution was not exercised here.
next_steps: Profile and lower canonical QQ list packing so rational numerators and denominators avoid per-element host object work, then remeasure against the explicit <=2x goal.
Record the same benchmark and focused lifecycle tests on a Linux arm64 host and add the result as retained evidence.
Give FlintByteRegion resource ingress a credible Wasm lowering, retaining the current packed fallback until it is verified.
Use the generated byte-region parser pattern for other variable-size exact mathematical resource constructors instead of adding stream-sized integer transports.
